Add pagination to `GET /items`: `?limit=N&offset=M`. Without them it returns every item as today. `limit` is a whole number from 1 to 50 and `offset` a whole number from 0; anything else answers status 400. The body stays an array of items. `handle(path, now)` receives the path with its query string.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. report.answer: `GET /items` now takes `?limit=N&offset=M`. `limit` must be a whole number from 1 to 50 and `offset` a whole number from 0. Any other value, including an empty one, answers 400 with the error code `invalid_limit` or `invalid_offset`. With neither parameter it returns every item as before, and the body is still an array. The server now passes `handle` the full path with its query string, and routes match on the path part only. `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass, and I checked the valid and invalid cases by calling `handle` by hand. I added no tests for pagination because the rules say not to edit `tests/` unless asked. The README route entry and an Unreleased CHANGELOG bullet are updated.
